name: Pyre

gist.Chaorc Ruin Mourner: Gets cheaper for each sacrifice this turn; then hits a target every time he sacrifices something, several times a turn.
gist.Chaorc Friendly Fireballer: Fetches a Fireball whenever he sacrifices; can sacrifice a creature to cast a Fireball itself.
gist.Chaorc Corpse Cannibal: Jumps into the slot of a sacrificed creature and draws a card on sacrifices.
gist.Chaorc Rider Warg: Reaction: when you kill one of his creatures it leaps in and the dead creature counts as sacrificed.
gist.Chaorc Pyre Grill Master: Sacrifices a creature to permanently raise the Attack or the health of every hero on the table.
gist.Chaorc Interception: Reaction: sacrifices a Chaorc to cancel an attack, spell or effect aimed at something else of his.
gist.Serket, Dread of the Desert: Gains a Prey Counter per sacrifice and once per turn hits a target for the whole pile of them.
gist.Rakah, the Loan Shark: Starts with no Attack; permanently gains the health of every small creature he sacrifices. Has Occultism to do the sacrificing.
gist.Calamitusk, the Chaorc War Chief: Sacrifices an older creature to summon a different Chaorc from hand or deck as a free action, a level cheaper.
gist.Occultism: Ability: sacrifice an older creature to hit a target.
gist.Chosen Sacrifice: Can be sacrificed from hand instead of a creature on the board, and replaces itself.
gist.Suspicious Monster: Enters by replacing a sacrificed creature.
gist.Fireball: Hits up to two of your targets.
gist.Heavy Hit: Rakah's attack once his Attack has grown; stuns.
gist.Chaorc Cannon Fodder: Can be sacrificed to Chaorc effects on the very turn it is summoned.

plan: Brant feeds his own creatures to the fire and gets paid for each one. A sacrifice is a hit from the Ruin Mourner, a Fireball from the Fireballer, a Prey Counter for Serket, permanent Attack for Rakah and a card from the Cannibal, all at once; Chosen Sacrifice, Cannon Fodder and Calamitusk keep the bodies coming. With the Rider Warg in hand, creatures you kill count as sacrifices too. After a few turns Serket and Rakah each hit like a truck every turn. The engine needs creatures that have survived a turn and it needs the Ruin Mourner; his three heroes have no defence other than Chaorc Interception.

looks.early: A few cheap Chaorcs and a Town Guard that he clearly intends to burn next turn.
looks.mid: Ruin Mourner and Friendly Fireballer side by side, creatures vanishing in threes, Prey Counters stacking on Serket.
looks.late: Rakah with a monstrous Attack, Serket's pile of counters, and hardly any creatures left because he has eaten them.

opening.tell: His creatures were all summoned this turn, and apart from the Cannon Fodder his sacrifice effects need creatures that have been out for a turn.
opening.why: For a turn or two the engine cannot run and his heroes stand in the open; every point of damage on them now is worth more than your own setup, because his damage only grows.

midgame.tell: A Chaorc Ruin Mourner stands at the back, and he is keeping one card ready whenever you look at his creatures.
midgame.why: With a Rider Warg in hand every creature you kill counts as a sacrifice and pays him; the Mourner is the multiplier, so take that one card (Dark Gear is clean; The Yeeting counts as a kill and lets the Warg in once) and leave the rest alone.

crisis.tell: Serket carries a pile of Prey Counters and Rakah's Attack has swollen; his board is nearly empty because he ate it.
crisis.why: The damage now comes from two heroes, one hit each per turn: freeze Rakah, hold Homerun! for Serket's shot, and put the rest into them. There is nothing left worth sweeping.

endgame.tell: He has no creatures left to sacrifice and his hand is empty.
endgame.why: The engine has burned itself out; Serket's counters stay, but with no new sacrifices nothing grows and his heroes are simply targets.

opening.board: Brant drops an Aggressive Town Guard and a Chaorc Corpse Cannibal and cracks his knuckles; nothing can be sacrificed until next turn.

options.text: Burn Rakah while the engine is cold

opening.board: A Friendly Fireballer arrives; he is clearly saving the Town Guard for it.
He sacrifices a Chosen Sacrifice from his hand to Occultism and stings your caster.

midgame.board: A Ruin Mourner lands almost for free after two sacrifices; each further one hits you.

options.text: Snow Cannon it and hit Serket
Sweep, into a waiting Rider Warg

midgame.board: You kill a Chaorc; a Rider Warg leaps out of his hand and the dead one counts as sacrificed, paying everything.

options.text: Stop killing fodder; remove the Mourner

midgame.board: The Pyre Grill Master raises the Attack of every hero on the table, yours included, which helps him far more.

crisis.board: Serket's counters are high and Rakah's Heavy Hit would nearly kill; he controls one creature.

options.text: Snow Cannon Rakah, Homerun! for Serket

crisis.board: A Fireball cast by the Fireballer itself hits two of your heroes.

options.text: Cloud in a Bottle, answer on Serket

crisis.board: Chaorc Interception is surely in his hand; he keeps a Chaorc untouched.

options.text: Untargeted damage: Storm and Chain Lightning
Bait it with a small spell
Aim your best spell at Serket

endgame.board: No creatures, no cards; Serket and Rakah both wounded.
Calamitusk trades his last creature for a Ruin Mourner with nothing to feed it.

options.text: Keep a shield for Serket's shot

endgame.board: Rakah alone, huge Attack, one Heavy Hit a turn.
